transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Jacob (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood AE), Priya (Horizon Head of Product), Derek (Eng Manager), Susan (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Patel, your CSM. Uh, quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya: Hi, Priya Rao here, Head of Product at Horizon.
[00:11] Derek: Derek Miles, engineering manager.
[00:13] Susan: Susan Park, security and compliance.
[00:15] Sofia: Sofia Chen from Redwood, will handle contracting and pricing.
[00:18] Jacob: Jacob Lee, solutions engineer, I'll run the tech deep dive later.
[00:22] Maya: Great, thanks. Agenda — we'll run through goals, timeline, security checklist, sandbox access, and pilot scope then capture next steps.

[02:01] Priya: Great. High-level for us: we want to get a pilot running with chat assistance and embeddings for semantic search within four weeks. Main constraints are data residency and SSO.

[02:35] Maya: Understood. Typical pilot — we do sandbox first, then a 2-week pilot in prod-ish environment. Does that align?

[03:10] Priya: Yes, prefer 4-week total: week 1 sandbox and integration, week 2-4 pilot with user testing.

[04:00] Derek: For infra, we need VPC peering or private deployment, because PHI-like data touch points. Are you able to do private deployments or VPC options?

[04:18] Jacob: Yes, Redwood supports VPC peering and we have the Redwood Private option — sometimes called Redwood Private or on-prem package — sorry, the auto transcription earlier calls it Red wood private — anyway, we can do VPC peering, and for pilots we often use a customer VPC with peering to our sandbox cluster or a dedicated sandbox in your cloud. We'll share the VPC peering checklist.

[05:05] Susan: From security we need SOC2 docs, encryption at rest with KMS/HSM, and SSO (SAML) + RBAC. Also audit logs retention — what are default retention windows?

[05:28] Maya: We'll send SOC2 report and our security package. KMS integration — we support customer-managed keys via KMS; HSM integrations possible for Private. Audit logs are available, default retention is 90 days for hosted but we can add longer retention as an add-on. We'll put specifics in the security packet.

[06:40] Susan: For data residency, we need EU-only processing for a subset of data. Is regional routing available?

[06:55] Jacob: Yes, our runtime supports region pinning and smart routing. For the pilot we can pin requests to the EU region. There might be slight latency tradeoffs but it keeps data residency compliance.

[08:12] Priya: Success metrics: latency p95 under 300ms for short prompts, embeddings index recall > 0.75 on our eval, and cost under $X per 1k requests — we'll formalize numbers.

[09:00] Maya: Good. For roles, who will be our day-to-day eng contact?

[09:07] Derek: That will be me. I'll also loop in two engineers who will do integration.

[10:00] Jacob: Technical notes — pilot scope: chat with function calling for structured responses, embeddings for semantic search, and small reranking. We'll provide a sandbox API key, and recommend continuous batching settings and a quantized model profile for cost savings.

[10:43] Derek: On quantization — are you recommending int8 or 4-bit? We are cautious about quality regression.

[10:55] Jacob: Typically we start with 8-bit quantization for pilots; we also provide quality baselines so you can see regressions. If you need higher fidelity we'll use FP16 model variants. We'll document tradeoffs.

[12:10] Susan: For logging, what level of PII is in logs by default? Do you do automatic redaction?

[12:22] Maya: By default we log tokens for debugging but we have masking and redaction options; we can disable storing request/response bodies in logs for regulated workflows. We'll include these options in the security packet.

[13:40] Priya: Great. Contracting question — Sofia, when can we get a pilot contract and pricing?

[13:48] Sofia: I'll prepare a pilot pricing worksheet and an MSA addendum for pilots. For pilot pricing we usually do a fixed seat or usage cap with an overage rate. I'll share a draft by end of week.

[14:15] Priya: Perfect. Also curious about Dedicated/reserved options after pilot.

[14:23] Maya: We can discuss Dedicated capacity after pilot — it'll be months out but we'll capture expected throughput and SLOs during the pilot.

[15:05] Derek: Network question — how do we handle private key exchange for KMS?

[15:15] Jacob: We'll provide a KMS integration guide; typically you'll configure a customer-managed key in your cloud KMS and give the service principal access. For HSM we have an integration path but it takes longer.

[16:30] Maya: Timeline recap: we'll get sandbox creds within 3 business days after you sign the pilot, tech deep dive next week, pilot kickoff once sandbox validated.

[18:00] Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? Susan: security review timelines?

[18:12] Susan: We'll need the SOC2 and network diagram to start our internal review. Likely 5-7 business days after receipt.

[19:00] Maya: We'll send SOC2 and network diagram today. Also the onboarding guide and the kickoff deck.

[20:30] Jacob: I'll propose times for the tech deep dive — I will focus on VPC peering, KV cache behavior, batching config, and model selection. Also we'll run a small benchmark script for your sample workload.

[22:05] Derek: That benchmark — will it be representative with token lengths ~200? Our prompts average 150-250 tokens.

[22:18] Jacob: Yes, we'll match token distribution, and provide p50/p95 latency and throughput numbers. For caching — we can show prefix caching improvements for repeated prompts.

[24:00] Priya: For pilot success, we want clear sign-off criteria: eng integration complete, latency and accuracy targets met, and security acceptance.

[24:17] Maya: Agreed — we'll capture that in the onboarding doc as success criteria.

[26:10] Sofia: On procurement — do you have a PO process? We accept purchase orders and can do vendor onboarding. I'll include the procurement checklist.

[27:30] Susan: Also will need an incident response contact and SLA details.

[27:44] Maya: We'll send incident response contacts and our SLA summary. For pilot SLOs we often give best-effort uptime and then add SLA after Dedicated.

[29:05] Derek: A couple of small technical clarifications: can we pin to model versions and avoid automatic model swaps during pilot?

[29:20] Jacob: Yes, you can pin model versions. We also support controlled rollouts but for pilot we'll pin to a stable model.

[31:00] Priya: Do you have pre-built embeddings pipelines or do we bring our own?

[31:10] Jacob: We have SDKs and reference pipelines for embeddings index building and vector stores integration; we can share example code and a sample notebook.

[33:45] Maya: Alright, recap and owners — Maya will send onboarding guide, SOC2, kickoff deck; Jacob will send sandbox setup and schedule tech deep dive; Sofia will send pilot pricing and procurement checklist; Priya/Derek will confirm pilot users and success metrics.

[34:20] Priya: One more question — do you have restrictions on training data usage? We need assurances that user data won't be used to train public models.

[34:35] Maya: Yes, we provide a clause: we won't use your data to train public models, and for Private deployments your data stays in your VPC. We'll include language in the MSA addendum.

[36:00] Susan: For the audit trail — can logs be exported to our SIEM?

[36:12] Jacob: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded via syslog or pushed into your logging endpoint; we'll include example configs.

[38:00] Priya: Okay that covers most items. When do you want to reconvene?

[38:12] Maya: Let's do a tech deep dive next Wednesday (2026-10-28) — I'll propose two time slots. Then pilot kickoff target 2026-11-01 pending internal approvals.

[40:00] Derek: Works for us.

[41:30] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll wait for the docs and SOC2.

[42:00] Maya: Thanks, will send a follow-up note with links and action items.

[52:00] Sofia: Thanks, bye.
